newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cap Gemini sees 700-800 mln Fr 98 profit,U.S. buys.
newsitem.headline: Cap Gemini sees 700-800 mln Fr 98 profit,U.S. buys.

text.p: French computer services company Cap Gemini expects a net profit of over 500 million francs ($85.9 million) this year and of 700-800 million francs the following year, chief executive Serge Kampf said in a newspaper interview.

Kampf told afternoon daily Le Monde the firm was happy that its major shareholder, Germany's Daimler-Benz, had decided to sell its stake in Cap Gemini. This would leave Cap Gemini free to develop and make acquisitions, notably in the United States.
"We will be able to pursue new geopgraphical developments and go ahead with acquisitions, notably in the United States," Kampf was quoted as saying in an interview.
"We've got out of our troubles of the past," he said. "Our net result should exceeed 500 million francs this year and come in around 700-800 million francs next year," he said.

Daimler said on Wednesday it would sell its 24.4 percent stake in the French computer systems and services company, killing speculation that it could take over the firm after six years as a large shareholder.
Daimler subsidiary Debis said on Thursday that it planned to recover an entire 1.3 billion marks investment which it had made in the French firm.

Kampf said Cap Gemini had been left in the dark on Daimler's intentions since an option to buy out the firm expired in 1996 and that the announcement came as a relief, also because of strategic differences.
Cap Gemini and Daimler had teamed up in computer services in Germany with the creation of Cap Debis in a "real test of our ability to work together".
"The result was that we ended up excluded from the German market," he said.

"Debis started to compete with us on our European markets, seeking last year to buy French firm GSI. We opposed this vehemently. Now Debis is a suitor to buy dutch firm Rocade. We are equally opposed," he said.

"The partnership over six years with Debis Systemhaus has not been as fruitful and we had hoped. Cultures and management methods are very different. Debis is much more geared towards heavy computer servies while we are closer to the consultancy domain," he said.
"Presence in the United States is of capital importance for us. Among the top 19 computer services firms in the world nine are American, the only exception is Cap Gemini, ranked fifth," he said.
Cap Gemini shares, which suffered from the open of the Paris stock exchange on Thursday, were down 5.62 percent at 325.6 francs at 1019 GMT.
